beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've brought a box to the meeting. Is this where you dismiss me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We want to discuss your promotion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Promotion to what? The box is very adaptable.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: More responsibility.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. I'll keep it for the mistakes.

card.title: Waiting for the Bad News
card.instruction: Treat pauses, changes, and uncertainty as signs that rejection or loss is approaching, then prepare yourself before it arrives.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You paused before answering. Shall I brace for goodbye?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was swallowing tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: People prepare their throats for difficult news.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm asking you to dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One last dinner, or may I leave the box at home?

card.title: Waiting for the Bad News
card.instruction: Treat pauses, changes, and uncertainty as signs that rejection or loss is approaching, then prepare yourself before it arrives.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the letter first. I'll decide whether today can hold it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's addressed to me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I know how crowded your day already is.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can handle my own news.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then let me handle the timing of your handling it.

card.title: Let Me Carry It
card.instruction: Take responsibility for managing everyone’s emotional burden, deciding what they should know, feel, and face.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've taken the difficult phone list. You rest.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Some of those people need to speak to me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll sort them by how upsetting they might be.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can't manage everyone's feelings.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not while you keep adding objections to the list.

card.title: Let Me Carry It
card.instruction: Take responsibility for managing everyone’s emotional burden, deciding what they should know, feel, and face.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're okay, aren't we? I can move my chair back.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We're okay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That sounded tired. Was the chair too close?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Stop changing everything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Is this the right distance for stopping?

card.title: Tell Me We’re Okay
card.instruction: Treat every response as evidence of whether you are still accepted, and adjust yourself quickly whenever reassurance feels incomplete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Was my joke too much? I'll change the ending.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine amused or fine tolerated?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I like you. Relax.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Should I relax with or without the joke?

card.title: Tell Me We’re Okay
card.instruction: Treat every response as evidence of whether you are still accepted, and adjust yourself quickly whenever reassurance feels incomplete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't call my disastrous opening heartbreaking. Call it excellent crowd management of no crowd.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was offering sympathy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Offer admiration. I stayed for the whole show.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Would a hug help?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As congratulations for endurance, perhaps.

card.title: Don’t Pity Me
card.instruction: Frame your struggle as evidence of strength, steering concern toward admiration and rejecting anything that feels like pity.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I carried the entire move myself. Please stop making that poor-you face.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You must be exhausted.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Impressively exhausted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I bring you tea?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. In the mug marked champion, not survivor.

card.title: Don’t Pity Me
card.instruction: Frame your struggle as evidence of strength, steering concern toward admiration and rejecting anything that feels like pity.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we close the old café, one minute's silence for the kettle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was only a kettle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It worked here longer than either of us. Stand properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I unplug it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After the minute. Don't interrupt its final shift.

card.title: The Proper Way to Grieve
card.instruction: Treat difficult feelings as requiring a precise ritual, sequence, or ceremony, and correct any attempt to rush or simplify it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We remember the garden in order: roses, apple tree, then the stubborn shed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could we just tell a story?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After the roses have their turn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My story involves the shed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then hold it respectfully until the tree has finished.

card.title: The Proper Way to Grieve

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You sighed at dinner. Should I stop the music?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ate too much.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Physical distress with emotional implications. I'll clear the table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please just sit down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Is sitting the intervention you need? I'll make a plan.

card.title: Emotional Emergency
card.instruction: Interpret every hesitation, sigh, or change in tone as the beginning of an emotional emergency requiring immediate intervention.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've crumpled your napkin. What changed in the last ten seconds?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wiped sauce off my chin.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Was the sauce disappointing?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine can be a warning word. I'll get water.

card.title: Emotional Emergency
card.instruction: Interpret every hesitation, sigh, or change in tone as the beginning of an emotional emergency requiring immediate intervention.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The gallery said they'd consider my paintings. I'll order opening-night glasses.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Consider doesn't mean yes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It means the door's open enough for glassware.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They say that to everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the art world's becoming wonderfully inclusive.

card.title: Hope Is Evidence
card.instruction: Treat every small kindness, coincidence, or improvement as undeniable proof that the best possible outcome is gathering momentum.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We've sold one book. The shop's turning a corner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You bought it yourself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: An informed customer recognised quality.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's still one sale.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. The first of a very clear sequence.

card.title: Hope Is Evidence
card.instruction: Treat every small kindness, coincidence, or improvement as undeniable proof that the best possible outcome is gathering momentum.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're upset. Water, quiet, or a walk?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Water won't fix this.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No. It makes being upset less thirsty.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want to explain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then quiet comes with the water. No questionnaire.

card.title: What Do You Need Now?
card.instruction: Accept every feeling as real, then translate it into water, space, a plan, a boundary, or the next practical step.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can be furious and still eat something. Toast?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can't think about food.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll put it here so thinking isn't required.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Don't tell me to calm down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I won't. Furious toast is still toast.

card.title: What Do You Need Now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your little wave had a pause in it. What did the pause mean?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was holding shopping.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then why did I feel dismissed between the bags?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was just a wave.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Recreate it without the pause. Let's compare.

card.title: That One Look
card.instruction: Choose one small look, phrase, silence, or gesture and treat it as the clearest evidence of what everything truly means.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You put a full stop after thanks. Is that where things end?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's punctuation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your usual thanks gets an exclamation mark.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was in a hurry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Enough hurry to remove enthusiasm. That's what I noticed.

card.title: That One Look
card.instruction: Choose one small look, phrase, silence, or gesture and treat it as the clearest evidence of what everything truly means.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You laughed at my joke. I'm calling today the beginning of the new chapter.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was a small joke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Important beginnings often arrive compactly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Shall we have tea?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our first tea after the turning point. Use different cups.

card.title: A Turning Point
card.instruction: Treat each emotional shift as proof that this moment will divide everything into before and after.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've written today's date in red. This is when I finally said no.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: To extra potatoes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The subject isn't the size of the boundary.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Would you like gravy?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Ask the new version of me.

card.title: A Turning Point
card.instruction: Treat each emotional shift as proof that this moment will divide everything into before and after.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

beats.text: You want me beside you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you planning to leave?

beats.text: I'm planning to stay without feeling trapped. Butter?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can stop when you need to.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Put the toast within reach. I can risk the first honest sentence now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Which question?

beats.speaker: A
